title.value: RegJEDI: A Joint-Embedding Diffusion Language Model for Regulatory DNA Design

data_release.value: We authorize the release of our submission and author names to the public in the event of acceptance.

TLDR.value: A fingerprint-conditioned diffusion language model for DNA design, with a training-only representation-alignment loss that improves conditional fidelity at no extra sampling cost.

abstract.value: Conditional generators for regulatory DNA design typically condition on a coarse label or a single activity score, collapsing a high-dimensional target onto one axis. We instead condition directly on a multi-assay functional fingerprint, treating design as a continuous, structured conditional generation problem, and release RegFP, a benchmark for it. RegJEDI is an absorbing-state discrete diffusion language model over DNA with a goal-separated denoiser: a goal-blind prefix processes the masked sequence and diffusion time, while a conditioned suffix injects the target fingerprint $P \in \mathbb{R}^{C \times A}$ via adaLN-Zero modulation and cross-attended profile tokens, with no reward model, reranking, or classifier guidance. We additionally introduce fREPA, a representation-alignment auxiliary loss that aligns intermediate features to a frozen target encoder during training only, removed at sampling. Against eight baselines spanning label-conditioned diffusion, reward-optimized generation, and fingerprint-conditioned controls, evaluated on held-out targets by an independent judge, RegJEDI achieves the best overall target fidelity and leads on most evaluation axes. Compared against an identically fingerprint-conditioned control at matched compute, fREPA alone yields a consistent, statistically reliable gain across most cell contexts — a cheap, general training-time lever for conditional generation on structured, high-dimensional targets with no added sampling cost. Evaluation is by an in-silico surrogate rather than wet-lab validation, and the mechanism behind the gain remains underdetermined.

TLDR.value: SDH formulates high-dimensional biomechanical control with local violations as a survival-based constrained RL problem and yields scalable, principled off-policy algorithms.

abstract.value: We propose stochastic decision horizons (SDH), a theoretically grounded framework for survival-based constrained reinforcement learning from per-step violation signals. Rather than treating violations as expenditure of a cumulative budget, SDH shortens the effective decision horizon when violations occur, reducing current reward credit and future bootstrapping. We show that this construction represents a geometric-horizon survival constraint and, for a fixed Lagrange multiplier, remains the same SDH problem up to a constant reward offset that acts as an implicit incentive for survival. Using control as inference, we derive two off-policy and replay-compatible, regularized algorithms with post-violation semantics. Absorbing-state ends the decision process, so only surviving decisions pay policy KL, yielding AS-SAC. Virtual termination stops reward credit while the process continues, retaining ordinary discounted KL and yielding VT-MPO. To connect SDH with cumulative-cost CMDPs, we introduce violation-depth profiles. Under exponential-tail single-scale profiles, the SDH statistic determines cumulative cost; departures from this form mark where the connection breaks. Experiments validate both the method and this predicted scope. On the 90-muscle H2190 humanoid in Hyfydy, VT-MPO matches the EWA reference in peak gait realism, with its highest observed gait-match checkpoint at 21M environment steps versus 90M for EWA and markedly more stable training. On Safety Gymnasium, violation-depth profiles predict the regimes in which SDH achieves strong reward-violation trade-offs.

title.value: Stochastic Decision Horizons for Survival-Based Constrained Reinforcement Learning

TLDR.value: SUBS parameterization-based Masked diffusion language models with function token conditioning show state-of-the-art performance over autoregressive models in conditional de novo protein sequence generation

abstract.value: The development of function-specific protein sequences is a critical challenge in the field of drug discovery and protein design. Current methods, including structure-based and protein language models, face limitations due to biases in structural predictions, the requirement for extensive fine-tuning, and difficulty in zero-shot generalization to unseen functional tasks. To address these challenges, we propose ProtDiff, a novel protein sequence diffusion model conditioned on function tokens. Unlike traditional protein generative models that rely on multimodal inputs or extensive fine-tuning, ProtDiff utilizes a masked diffusion language modeling approach with classifier-free guidance to generate protein sequences in a zero-shot manner solely based on a predefined function token vocabulary. The idffusion process leverages an absorbing state forward process where protein sequences transition to a masked state, allowing a small transformer-based backbone model to iteratively reconstruct sequences. By training on InterPro datasets and employing a classifier-free diffusion guidance mechanism, ProtDiff demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in functional adaptation and de novo sequence generation tasks compared to existing models. Evaluation on both function-matching and de novo generation benchmarks shows that ProtDiff effectively generates novel, stable protein sequences that conform to specified functional constraints, showing comparable results to autoregressive model equivalents with higher parameter counts. Our results indicate that ProtDiff not only advances the state-of-the-art in protein design but also opens new avenues for explainable and targeted protein generation for drug discovery applications.

title.value: ProtDiff: Function-Conditioned Masked Diffusion Models for Robust Directed Protein Generation
